info.name: VN Stock Sim API
info.description:
Every route the Go + Gin backend exposes under /api/v1, generated from the actual handler/types source (backend/internal/*), not api-spec.md's intent document, so field names and bindings here are exactly what the code accepts today. See RESUME.md for what is mock/in-memory vs. real.

Quick start:
1. Set the `baseUrl` collection variable (defaults to http://localhost:8080, i.e. `go run ./cmd/api` or the Docker Compose backend service reached from the host).
2. Run "Auth > Register" (or "Auth > Login" if the account already exists) once -- its test script saves the returned accessToken into the `accessToken` collection variable automatically, and every other authenticated request inherits it via collection-level Bearer auth.
3. Public endpoints (Symbols, Market, Screener) work with no token.
4. "Portfolio > List Portfolios", "Orders > Create Order (Market)", and "Backtests > Create Backtest" each save an id (portfolioId/orderId/backtestId) into collection variables for the requests below them that need one.

exec: // Computed fresh before every request so date-ranged market endpoints
// (bars/indicators) work out of the box with no manual editing --
// matches api-spec.md's from/to being unix seconds.

item.name: Auth
item.description: backend/internal/auth. Register/Login are public; Me requires the bearer token the other two return.

request.description: 201 on success -> { accessToken, expiresIn, user }. 409 email_taken if this email was already registered (in-memory store resets on backend restart).
200 on success -> { accessToken, expiresIn, user }. 401 invalid_credentials otherwise.
Re-verifies the bearer token against the store on every call (no local JWT decoding) -> { id, email, displayName }.

item.name: Symbols
item.description: backend/internal/symbol + insight. All public (no auth) -- they back the stock browser/chart before login.

query.description: matches symbol or company name, case-insensitive

request.description: -> { data: Symbol[], meta: {page,pageSize,totalItems,totalPages} }. V1 mock universe: VNM, VCB, HPG, FPT, SHB.
-> Symbol + lastPrice/change/changePercent (live, derived from market bars) + marketCap/peRatio/pbRatio/eps/dividendYield + reference/ceiling/floor (HOSE +-7% / HNX +-10% / UPCOM +-15% price bands).
-> { symbol, summary, signals[], source: "rule-based", generatedAt }. Deliberately NOT a real LLM call -- see RESUME.md.

item.name: Market
item.description: backend/internal/market. All public. Bars/indices/orderbook are deterministic (pure functions of symbol+time), not a random walk -- repeated calls a few seconds apart return identical numbers for the same instant.

request.description: -> { data: Bar[] } (time/open/high/low/close/volume).

query.description: sma | ema | rsi -- Bollinger/VWAP are not implemented (V1 scope is only what design/screens/Detail.dc.html's chart shows)

request.description: -> { data: IndicatorPoint[] } (time/value).
-> { data: IndicatorPoint[] }, Wilder-smoothed RSI, values in [0,100]. Added Phase D for the Detail screen's RSI(14) panel.

-> { data: IndicatorMultiPoint[] }, each { time, values: { macd, signal, histogram } }. Added Phase D for the Detail screen's MACD(12,26,9) panel -- doesn't fit the single-value IndicatorPoint shape the other indicators use, hence its own endpoint.
-> { data: IndexSnapshot[] } for VN-Index, VN30, HNX-Index, UPCOM-Index -- each { name, value, change, changePercent, sparkline[] }.
-> { data: { bids: PriceLevel[], asks: PriceLevel[] } }, 6 levels each side, 100 VND tick (hardcoded simplification -- see RESUME.md Phase B notes).
backend/internal/screener -> { data: SectorGroup[] }, each { sector, avgChangePercent, tickers: TickerChange[] }.

Phase I: period = 1D | 1W | 1M | 3M (change over 1/5/21/63 sessions of daily bars), exchange = ALL | HOSE | HNX | UPCOM. Sectors and tiles come back sorted by market cap, with up/down/flat breadth per sector.

exec: pm.test('only HOSE tiles', () => pm.response.json().data.forEach(g => g.tickers.forEach(t => pm.expect(t.exchange).to.eql('HOSE'))));

request.description: Unknown period -> 400 validation_error.
backend/internal/screener -> { data: TickerChange[] } (symbol, changePercent, price, volume), sorted by changePercent.
-> { timestamp } (unix seconds).

item.name: Watchlist
item.description: backend/internal/watchlist. Authenticated, per-user (not per-portfolio -- see RESUME.md Phase B decision 2).

request.description: -> { data: Item[] } (symbol, addedAt, lastPrice, change, changePercent, volume).
Idempotent (adding an already-watched symbol is a no-op). -> { data: Item[] }, the full updated list.
204 No Content, whether or not the symbol was actually on the list.
Unknown symbols are refused (Phase K; before, any string was stored).
Pairs by their full name. Items carry companyName and exchange ("CRYPTO" for pairs).

exec: pm.test('pair listed with its name', () => { const i = pm.response.json().data.find(x => x.symbol === 'BTCUSDT'); pm.expect(i.exchange).to.eql('CRYPTO'); pm.expect(i.companyName).to.eql('Bitcoin'); });

item.name: Portfolio
item.description: backend/internal/portfolio. Authenticated. /portfolio (singular) always resolves to the caller's lazily-created default portfolio; /portfolios (plural) is the real multi-portfolio API from Phase B.

request.description: -> { cashBalance, marketValue, totalEquity, unrealizedPnl, unrealizedPnlPercent } for the default portfolio (auto-created with 100,000,000 VND on first call).
-> { data: Position[] } (symbol, quantity, avgCost, lastPrice, marketValue, unrealizedPnl) for the default portfolio.
-> { data: Portfolio[] } -- every portfolio the caller owns (at least the default one).

All fields optional -- omitted name/market/currency fall back to "Danh muc moi"/"stock"/"VND", omitted or <=0 startingCapital falls back to 100,000,000. market: "stock" | "crypto" (crypto portfolios aren't tradable yet, Phase I). -> 201 Portfolio.
404 if portfolioId doesn't exist or belongs to another user. Run "List Portfolios" or "Create Portfolio" first to populate {{portfolioId}}.
Same shape as "Get Default Portfolio Summary" but for any owned portfolio by id -- useful for confirming two portfolios' balances stay isolated.
Phase E addition. One (timestamp, nav) point per fill against this portfolio, plus a seed point at creation -- backs the Portfolio screen's equity-curve chart.
Phase E addition. Current NAV grouped by sector (via the existing symbol data) plus a trailing "Tiền mặt" (cash) bucket -- backs the Portfolio screen's sector allocation bars.

Phase E addition. Real KPIs (win rate, profit factor, max drawdown, avg win/loss, best/worst trade) computed by FIFO-matching this portfolio's actual filled buy/sell orders into closed trades -- backs the Portfolio screen's KPI row and journal grid.

item.name: Orders
item.description: backend/internal/order. Authenticated paper-trading orders. "market" fills immediately against the current mock quote; "limit"/"atc"/"stop" are accepted and stored "queued" (no matching engine yet in V1).

request.description: -> { data: Order[] } for the caller, across all their portfolios.

portfolioId is optional -- omit it to use the caller's default portfolio. side: buy | sell. type: market fills immediately and returns filledPrice + a 0.15% fee. 409 insufficient_funds / insufficient_shares if the paper account can't cover it. -> 201 Order.

price is the requested limit/stop trigger price (Phase E addition -- previously collected by the order ticket UI but never sent to or stored by the backend). type can also be "atc" or "stop" (LO/ATC/Stop from the design's order ticket) -- since Phase K a background matcher fills them against 5-minute bars (limit/stop when touched, ATC at the 14:45 close, OCO one leg; phase-k.md), and one already marketable at the current price fills at once. This one (20,000, far below the price) stays "queued", fee 0. Its test script overwrites {{orderId}} with this queued order's id (not the market order's above), so the default top-to-bottom run demonstrates a real successful Cancel below rather than a 409.
{{orderId}} is whichever of the two Create Order requests above ran last -- run either one first to populate it.

Only a still-"queued" order can be cancelled. In the default top-to-bottom run, {{orderId}} points at the "Create Order (Limit, queued)" order, so this succeeds; re-running it against a filled market order's id (or cancelling twice) returns 409 cannot_cancel instead.
Orders are only accepted into a portfolio the caller owns -- an unknown or another user's portfolioId returns 404 portfolio_not_found (phase-g.md decision 3).
limit and stop orders need a price (Phase K).

item.name: Create Order (marketable limit fills at once)

request.description: A buy limit at or above the current price is marketable: it fills immediately at that price, with the fee taken from cash (phase-k.md decisions 1 and 6).

exec: pm.test('filled at the current price with a fee', () => { const o = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(o.status).to.eql('filled'); pm.expect(o.filledPrice).to.be.below(999999999); pm.expect(o.fee).to.be.above(0); });

item.name: Backtests
item.description: backend/internal/backtest. Authenticated. Runs synchronously today (the response shape already matches api-spec.md's async queue-then-poll contract for when a real worker pool lands). V1 only supports one rule: ema_crossover.

request.description: from/to are YYYY-MM-DD (not unix seconds, unlike the market endpoints). rule.params.fast/slow default to 20/50 if omitted or <=0. -> 202 Backtest { id, symbol, status: "completed", finalCapital, returnPercent, totalTrades, winRate }.

Phase H rule (phase-h.md decision 3): buy when RSI(period) crosses up through entry (and price > SMA(trendSma) if set), sell when RSI > exit or the price is stopLossPercent below entry. Both rules now also return maxDrawdownPercent and profitFactor.
Run "Create Backtest" first to populate {{backtestId}}.
The single-backtest endpoint carries per-bar equity next to buy-and-hold, the trade list, and the run inputs (Phase K /backtest page); the list endpoint leaves equity and trades out.

exec: pm.test('equity, benchmark and inputs', () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.equity.length).to.be.above(10); pm.expect(b.equity[0]).to.have.keys('time','equity','benchmark'); pm.expect(b).to.have.property('benchmarkReturnPercent'); pm.expect(b.startingCapital).to.be.above(0); });

item.name: Replay
item.description: backend/internal/replay (Phase F). Authenticated. Each session gets its own dedicated portfolio (created automatically) so historical replay fills never mix with the user's real paper-trading account -- see phase-f.md decision 4. A fill always executes at the currently-revealed candle's close; there is no price field to send. Run "Start Session" first to populate {{replaySessionId}}.

request.description: resolution/totalBars/startDate are all optional -- default to "1D"/120/"2021-01-04" (matching design/screens/Replay.dc.html's own caption exactly). -> 201 SessionView with the first 20 candles already revealed.
A Replay session's portfolio (kind: "replay") only receives fills from its own session; a live POST /orders into it returns 409 replay_portfolio (phase-g.md decision 4).

stopLoss is optional and only meaningful on a buy -- if the low of a later revealed candle breaches it, Advance auto-sells the whole position at the stop price. Fills always at Bars[currentBar-1].Close, never a client-supplied price.
Reveals the next candle. Safe to call repeatedly past the last candle (done stays true, no error).

Callable at any point, not just once all candles are revealed -- an early exit is scored over however many bars were actually played. result.skill.final becomes true; it's already present (and honest about only using revealed bars) on every response before this, per the design's "provisional score" panel.

item.name: Crypto
item.description: Phase I (docs/roadmap/phases/phase-i.md): backend/internal/crypto. Public market data from Binance (MARKET_DATA_SOURCE=vci) with a deterministic mock fallback; every quote carries source: binance | mock. Crypto wallets are portfolios with market=crypto (10,000 USDT, fractional quantities, 0.10% fee).

request.description: -> { data: PairQuote[] } for the 24 pairs in 4 categories.
Accepts BTCUSDT, BTC-USDT or BTC. -> PairDetail (adds allTimeHigh, distanceFromAthPercent, volatility30dPercentDay).
Unknown pair -> 404 not_found.
interval = 5m | 15m | 1h | 4h | 1d | 1w; from/to unix seconds. -> { data: Bar[], source }.
levels per side (default 4, max 20); each level { price, size, cumulative }.

exec: pm.test('4 + 4 levels', () => { const d = pm.response.json().data; pm.expect(d.bids.length).to.eql(4); pm.expect(d.asks.length).to.eql(4); });

request.description: Same SectorGroup shape as /market/heatmap, grouped by coin category, 24h change.
direction = up | down.
BTC/ETH quotes + sparklines, total market cap of the 24 pairs, dominance.
market=crypto -> currency USDT, default capital 10,000. Does not change the stock default portfolio.
Quantity may be fractional (rounded to 8 decimals); fee 0.10% of fill value.

exec: pm.test('filled, 0.10% fee', () => { const o = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(o.status).to.eql('filled'); pm.expect(o.fee).to.be.closeTo(o.filledPrice * 0.025 * 0.001, 0.01); });

request.description: type oco needs both price (limit) and stopPrice; queued like limit/stop.

exec: pm.test('queued with both prices', () => { const o = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(o.status).to.eql('queued'); pm.expect(o.stopPrice).to.eql(1); });

request.description: A stock ticker into a crypto wallet (or a pair into a stock portfolio) -> 409 wrong_market.
Stocks trade whole shares only.
market=crypto: 1h bars from 2021-05-01, its own 10,000 USDT replay portfolio.

exec: pm.test('hourly USDT session', () => { const s = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(s.market).to.eql('crypto'); pm.expect(s.startingCapital).to.eql(10000); });

item.name: Quant
item.description: backend/internal/quant (Phase H). Authenticated. Bring-your-own-key: every request carries the user's own model key (provider claude | openai | custom), which is used for that one call and never stored or logged. The model only turns the question into structured conditions / a strategy draft; the backend runs them against its own data. These requests are written to pass without a real key (they assert the error paths); put your own key in apiKey to see a real answer. See docs/roadmap/phases/phase-h.md.

request.description: One real round trip on the sample question 'Lọc HOSE có RSI dưới 35 và ROE trên 15%.' -> 200 { ok, latencyMs, usage, understood, expected: 3, labels, models }. With an empty apiKey it fails fast with 400 missing_connection and no model call. A wrong key returns 502 provider_error with the provider's own message and providerStatus.

body.raw:
{
  "provider": "custom",
  "baseUrl": "ftp://169.254.169.254/v1",
  "model": "any",
  "messages": [{ "role": "user", "content": "Lọc HOSE có RSI dưới 35 và ROE trên 15%" }],
  "scope": { "prices": true, "indicators": true, "watchlist": true, "positions": false },
  "defaultExchange": "HOSE"
}

request.description: Self-hosted endpoints are user-supplied URLs the server connects to, so only http(s) URLs are accepted and loopback/private/link-local addresses (e.g. http://169.254.169.254) are refused with 400 endpoint_not_allowed unless the backend runs with QUANT_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS=true. This example uses a non-http scheme so it is refused under either setting. On success: 200 { reply, screen: { labels, universe, matches[] }, strategy, dropped[], plan, usage, latencyMs, model, temperatureApplied }.
